title: Quant Convergence — Graham Value Rules as ML Noise Filter on H198
description: arXiv:2606.24575 (Yamazaki & Garrido-Lestache, Jun 2026) tests Benjamin Graham's classic value rules as a 'low-pass filter' on ML models trained on 20 years of S&P 500 data. Key finding: pure Graham Random Forest achieves 232.13% return (2022-2026) with 1.38 Calmar Ratio — outperforming complex AutoGluon (222.68%) which suffered a 39.78% drawdown from overweighting volatile tech. Graham rules include: P/E < 15, P/B < 1.5, Current Ratio > 2.0, Long-Term Debt/Net-Current-Assets < 1.0, EPS growth 10yr positive. H466 applies Graham rules as a pre-filter on H198's 30-stock NASDAQ large-cap universe before the 6-1m momentum ranking step. This tests whether momentum signals on Graham-quality stocks (value + quality composite) produce better OOS Sharpe than pure momentum. Variants: A (Graham P/E<15 + P/B<1.5 filter, then top-6 by momentum), B (Combined RF: momentum rank + Graham score composite), C (Pure Graham rank, top-6), D (H198 momentum baseline top-6), E (H198 6-0m no-skip baseline). Data: FMP API for P/E, P/B, current ratio, debt data — quarterly refresh with 90-day reporting lag applied. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.174 (H198 baseline) AND MaxDD improvement. IS: 2013-2020, OOS: 2021-2026. NOTE: Graham filters on NASDAQ large-cap universe are likely very restrictive — large-cap tech stocks rarely have P/E<15 or P/B<1.5. Expect low n in universe after filter. May need to relax to P/E<25 to maintain sufficient universe size. Key question: does any Graham filter add value on a universe already dominated by quality growth stocks (where Graham's margin-of-safety logic may not apply)?
content:
# H466 — Quant Convergence: Graham Rules as ML Low-Pass Filter on H198

## Source
arXiv:2606.24575 (Yamazaki & Garrido-Lestache, Jun 2026) 'Quant Convergence: Bridging Classical Value Investing and Modern Factor Models for Systematic Equity Selection'

## Key Paper Findings
- Graham Random Forest: 232.13% return (2022-2026), Calmar Ratio 1.38 — highest risk-adjusted
- Complex AutoGluon: 222.68% return but 39.78% drawdown (bought volatile tech pre-crash)
- Combined Random Forest (momentum + Graham): 202.91% return, lowest MaxDD of any model tested
- Graham rules act as 'low-pass filter' suppressing momentum model noise
- Test window March 2022 - March 2026: includes 2022 crash and tech recovery — stress test period
- Key Graham metrics: P/E < 15, P/B < 1.5, Current Ratio > 2.0, LTD/NCA < 1.0, 10yr EPS growth positive

## H198 Adaptation
- Universe: H198 30-stock NASDAQ large-cap
- Note: Graham P/E<15 filter will be extremely restrictive on NASDAQ large-cap (AAPL P/E~30, MSFT~35)
- Relaxed Graham proxy: (a) P/E < 35 (sector-relative), (b) P/B < 5, (c) positive 3yr EPS CAGR
- Data source: FMP API ($FMP_API_KEY available) for quarterly fundamentals with 90-day reporting lag

## Variants
- A: Strict Graham filter (P/E<15, P/B<1.5), then 6-1m momentum on surviving stocks
- B: Relaxed Graham (P/E<35, P/B<5, positive 3yr EPS), then 6-1m momentum top-6
- C: Combined RF approach: 0.6×momentum_rank + 0.4×graham_quality_score, top-6
- D: Pure Graham quality rank, top-6 (no momentum) — standalone value test
- E: H198 6-1m momentum baseline, top-6

## Gate
- OOS Sharpe > 1.174 (H198 baseline)
- MaxDD improvement vs baseline (primary value: risk reduction)
- WF ratio 0.75-2.5

## IS/OOS Split
- IS: 2013-2020
- OOS: 2021-2026

## Cost
- FMP API: already available ($FMP_API_KEY)
- Fundamental data download: ~$0 additional cost (bulk quarterly download)

## Script
backtesting/daily/run_h466_graham_ml_filter.py

## CAUTION
- Graham strict filters likely eliminate all 30 H198 stocks (tech universe incompatible with P/E<15)
- Primary hypothesis test: relaxed Graham filters (Var B) as quality screen
- Cross-reference: H337 quality factor (GP/A, ROE) NOT CONFIRMED on H198 — same root cause
  likely: 30-stock large-cap universe has no cross-sectional quality variation
